svg.text: INSTRUCTIONAL MOCKUP — NOT A LIVE CAPTURE OR RESULT
Know the real DoD and STIG boundaries
Your Windows host · Notepad lab notes
External practice user
Firewall / private lab boundary
RHEL 9 DMZ application server
NGINX · TLS ends here
Hosted practice application
EXPECTED RESULT / SIMULATED CLUE — CHECK YOUR OWN MACHINE
Your notes identify the appropriate policy owners and say this is isolated simulated-CA
training.
FOLLOW THE NUMBERED INSTRUCTIONS IN THE LESSON
1. Open the official DoD PKI/PKE and DISA STIG resources linked in the course references. Ask the
organization’s PKI and security owners which current profiles apply.
2. A non-person entity certificate identifies a service or device. A server TLS certificate is not a CAC
user certificate and does not enable CAC sign-in by itself.
3. Real controls may cover approved issuers, algorithms, key protection, certificate policies,
revocation checking, allowed protocols, audit records and system crypto configuration.
4. Use the current applicable RHEL, web-server and organizational guidance. This lab is not DoD-approved
PKI, not a STIG scan, and not a claim of FIPS validation. Do not weaken the installed crypto policy to
make an example connect.
5. Revocation means the issuer marks a certificate as no longer acceptable before its expiry. A CRL is a
published revocation list; OCSP is a status-checking service. Our simple practice CA publishes neither,
so real revocation checks need your approved enterprise PKI design.
No real private key, real certificate result, production access or DoD endorsement is shown.
